title: Oxygen — Limitations
abstract: Flight crew limitations for the oxygen system, covering the minimum crew oxygen pressure for dispatch, its dependence on cabin temperature and the passenger oxygen provisions.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the flight crew limitations for the crew and passenger oxygen systems, including the dispatch pressure and how it is read.
sections.description: The crew oxygen system must show at least the minimum pressure for the number of occupants and the planned route before departure. The indicated pressure varies with cylinder temperature, so the reading taken on a cold morning is not the same as the reading taken on the same cylinder in the afternoon, and the dispatch table is entered with both the indication and the temperature. Reading the indication alone against a single figure will occasionally reject a serviceable cylinder and, more rarely, accept one that is short. Passenger oxygen is supplied by chemical generators and there is no pressure to check; the crew confirmation is limited to the door and the reset state shown on the panel. Where the aircraft is dispatched with the crew oxygen at or close to the minimum, the crew should be aware that the margin above the requirement is small and that a diversion at altitude will consume it quickly.
sections.crew_procedure: Before departure, read the crew oxygen indication and the cylinder temperature and enter the dispatch table with both. Do not accept a cylinder on the indication alone. Confirm the passenger oxygen panel shows the system reset and the doors closed. If the indication is below the table value, do not depart; a cylinder that is genuinely low cannot be topped up from the flight deck and the aircraft needs a charging trolley.
sections.limitation_note: Dispatch is not permitted with crew oxygen below the pressure given in the dispatch table for the number of occupants, the planned cruise altitude and the recorded cylinder temperature. The table, not a single pressure figure, is the limitation.

type_data.crew_action: Read pressure and cylinder temperature and enter the dispatch table with both.
